title: Plugins
goal: Host CLAP on both targets and VST3, AU and LV2 through JUCE inside the graph, with latency compensation, state, capabilities and crash survival.

humanGates.text: Choose the third-party plugins used for compatibility runs.
humanGates.how: The maintainer lists installed plugins; pluginval-checked runs use them.

features.title: CLAP host for both targets
acceptance: ClapPluginHost loads CLAP plugins in the desktop and headless builds; sample-accurate parameter events; latency and state through the PluginHost contract.

features.title: Plugin slots in the document and PluginNode in the graph
acceptance: plugin.instantiate (job) then plugin.insert (pure command) with a state blob; missing plugins show as missing with state preserved; instances survive unrelated edits through the pinned instance table.

PluginNode calls PluginInstance::process only from a GraphDriver callback or from the offline driver during bounce and export, never both at once; the driver's CallbackTimer covers the realtime path. Test: a hosted test plugin whose block exceeds its period counts as an xrun in the driver's timing (ADR-0018, condition 1).

The plugin event sink and the adapter's listener code only push to pluginEventAny (never setState, setParameter, device control or any wait for the audio thread: they run under JUCE's processMutex and listenerLock); the consumer of pluginEventAny runs on the command thread. Test: a plugin that reports from inside a restart and from the audio thread leaves the audio thread running (spec, "Threads and waiting rules"; ADR-0018, condition 2).

MIDI output has a recorded decision before a MIDI-producing plugin processes audio: the node preallocates its MIDI buffer for Steinberg's 2048-event limit and accepts JUCE's Array growth as plugin-caused, or MIDI-producing plugins wait for worker processes (ADR-0018, condition 3). Test for the first option: a plugin emitting more events than the preallocated size is measured and reported; for the second: loading a MIDI-producing plugin is refused.

The protocol carries xruns, maxCallbackMicros and unmeasuredCallbacks in the engine's status once the engine process runs a device, with a test that drives a known miss through to a client (ADR-0018, condition 4).

features.title: Hostile test plugin
acceptance: A built-in CLAP test plugin that allocates, throws, changes latency, sleeps and calls back into the host; the engine survives each behaviour with the documented outcome.

features.title: VST3, AU and LV2 through JUCE
acceptance: JucePluginHost formats behind the same PluginHost interface; capability flags exposed to agents; pluginval runs on the chosen plugins.

The spec's audit of what JUCE runs inside processBlock (locks, and the allocation MIDI output can cause) is repeated for the JUCE pin in use and for LV2 before the pin moves or the format ships; a lock or allocation the audit does not list reopens ADR-0018.

features.title: Plugin crash recovery
acceptance: A plugin crash during playback leaves the UI alive; the engine restarts and recovers the session from checkpoint plus journal.

exit.text: Third-party plugins load, save state, compensate latency and survive restart; capability flags are exposed to agents.
exit.how: Plugin tests plus pluginval runs on the chosen plugins.
